column1: # The divergence.broiler-js and divergence.broiler-vm fields corpus revision 26 retires: every Temporal vector
# Broiler.JS matches after milestone SJL-10.5's cut-over, under TZ=UTC and under TZ=America/New_York, in the runs
# on revision 25 at 6dbff805, whose code the branch's merge of main, e2b2a785, leaves unchanged
# (Broiler.JS/CHANGELOG.md lists the corrections and the policy changes); and every one Broiler.VM matches after
# milestone SJL-10.4's, in its run on revision 25 at its 9b7eead (its JSD-0079 lists the correction, and its
# bundle sjl-10-001 section 4 records the run); under the reason scripts/conformance/temporal-divergences.txt gave
# it at revision 25. The reasons' text follows the table.

# js-r7: row R7: integer narrowing inside addition (the milestone's listed correction): a year sum cast to int wraps (2020-06-15T12:00 + P4294967295Y is 2019-06-15T12:00, and so for PlainYearMonth and for Hebrew and Coptic dates) and a time added to a date or date-time saturates at a long (2020-01-01 plus 9e24 ns is 2312-04-11), where CalendarDateAdd's ISODateWithinLimits and the time duration's limit throw a RangeError; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-b5: row B5: a year-month's addition is checked against the year-month limits only, so -271821-05 - P1M is -271821-04, where AddDurationToYearMonth adds to the first of the month through CalendarDateAdd, whose ISODateWithinLimits refuses -271821-04-01; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-d3: row D3: Duration.prototype.add and subtract with calendar units (the milestone's listed correction): with a relativeTo they throw a plain Error, "not yet implemented", where AddDurations throws a RangeError for a calendar unit; and a second argument is read as options (5 and null a TypeError, a relativeTo getter run), where add and subtract take one parameter; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-d4: row D4: compare adds the whole duration, time included, to relativeTo and requires a representable date-time, so durations whose seconds DateDurationDays and the time duration's bound admit throw a RangeError, where compare answers 1; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-d6: row D6: rounding to months adds the rounded month count to relativeTo and re-derives years and months with DiffCalendarDate, so from 2020-01-31 fifteen months, a clamped 2021-04-30, read P1Y2M30D, where RoundRelativeDuration keeps the nudge's P1Y3M and bubbles it; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-d7: row D7: rounding to months relative to a plain date whose destination lies past the first window re-derives through a clamped difference (row D6's path), so {months: 10, days: 29, hours: 12} from 2019-03-31 is P10M29D, where the pinned text answers P11M (decision D7); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-d8: row D8: rounding relative to a zoned date takes the window's end as the nudged instant whenever the window was shifted, so {months: 10, days: 29, hours: 12} from 2019-03-31T00:00[UTC] bubbles into P1Y, where the pinned text keeps the window's start and answers P11M (decision D7: the text rules over its polyfill, which answers P1Y); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-d11: row D11: relativeTo in another calendar: round, total and compare throw a plain Error, "a relativeTo with the ... calendar is not yet implemented", where GetTemporalRelativeToOption takes any calendar; and a ZonedDateTime relativeTo in coptic rounds with ISO months (P1M14D for P1M15D), which the row does not record; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-f4: row F4: differences in another calendar ignore the rounding options (PlainDate, PlainYearMonth and ZonedDateTime) or measure months in ISO (PlainDateTime), so Hebrew 2020-01-01 until 2020-07-20 rounded to months is P6M24D, where it is P7M (the milestone's listed correction); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-f7: row F7: ZonedDateTime until and since with a calendar smallest unit nudge on 24-hour days, so New York's 23- and 25-hour days round as if they had 24 (2026-03-07T12:00 until 23:45 is PT0S, where it is P1D), where NudgeToCalendarUnit measures the window in the zone's instants (the milestone's listed DST correction); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g3: row G3: a year-month string's day is captured and validated only outside ISO 8601 and the Gregorian family, so a year-month whose day is not a date (2020-02-30, 2020-01-00, 2021-02-29) is read as its year-month, where DateSpec's early error makes it a RangeError; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g4: row G4: PlainTime's parser matches a date-time's date as any two digits and never validates it, so the time of 2021-13-45T12:00 or 2020-02-30T12:00 is 12:00:00, where the date must be a date; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g6: row G6: the instant pattern makes each time separator optional on its own, so 12:3045 and 1230:45 read as 12:30:45, where each time is in one form; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g8: row G8: PlainDate, PlainDateTime, PlainYearMonth and PlainMonthDay match an offset after a time without its range, so +24:00, +23:60 and +23:59:60 are accepted, where UTCOffset's hour is 00 to 23 and its minute and second 00 to 59; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g9: row G9: digits are matched with .NET's \d, which admits every Unicode decimal digit, and int.Parse then lets a FormatException escape the evaluation (in the four plain types' offset the digits are accepted and the offset ignored), where the grammar's DecimalDigit is ASCII and the string a RangeError; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g11: row G11: an empty or flag-only annotation, [] or [!], counts as a time zone annotation and is not checked, so it is accepted after a date-time, where it is neither a time zone identifier nor a key-value pair; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g12: row G12: a time zone annotation's text is checked only for a sub-minute offset, so [Mars Olympus], [ UTC], [UTC ], [/a], [a/], [a//b], [9a] and [+24:00] are accepted outside ZonedDateTime, where TimeZoneIdentifier refuses them; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g13: row G13: a time zone annotation after another annotation is accepted and the zone taken wherever it stands, where AnnotatedDateTime puts the time zone annotation first; correction (the area design's annotations in the wrong order), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g16: row G16: the year-month pattern lets a time follow an optional day, so 2020-01T12:00 and its basic and space forms read as 2020-01, where AnnotatedYearMonth has no time; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g17: row G17: a calendar string is read by TemporalIsoString.TryParse, which refuses none of the strings ParseTemporalCalendarString refuses (a time with Z, a year-month or month-day with a calendar, an empty, unknown critical or misplaced annotation, an offset out of range) and of several u-ca annotations answers the last, where the first rules; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g18: row G18: CanonicalizeTimeZone falls back to extracting a zone from any string, so T10:00Z, 10:00Z and 1214Z answer UTC and a time zone annotation after another, or the last of two, is taken, where ParseTemporalTimeZoneString refuses them; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g19: row G19: Z and z are accepted as an offset string in with() and in a property bag, where ToOffsetString takes UTCOffset[+SubMinutePrecision], which has no Z; correction (the area design's table), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-g20: row G20: a relativeTo string is read by TryParseRelative, which accepts a time zone annotation after another annotation (row G13) and an offset out of range (+25:00), where GetTemporalRelativeToOption's grammar refuses both; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5
# js-g22: row G22: a duration's time designator with no time part (P1YT, P1DT, P1Dt) is accepted, where DurationTime needs a part; correction (a lenient grammar acceptance), answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c2: row C2: the aliases gregorian and minguo are accepted as gregory and roc, by the constructor, an annotation and a calendar string, where Table 1's aliases are ethiopic-amete-alem and islamicc only (decision D5); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c5: row C5: an invalid month code under constrain (M00, M13 where there is no thirteenth month, M14, M99) is constrained to the first or the last month in Coptic, Ethiopic, Indian, the Islamic calendars and Persian, where NonISOResolveFields throws a RangeError for a month code the calendar lacks (the milestone's listed correction); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c6: row C6: a month code with decimal digits other than ASCII passes ^M\d{2}L?$ and int.Parse then lets a FormatException escape the evaluation, where MonthCode's digits are ASCII and the code a RangeError; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c9: row C9: era names of earlier drafts and aliases the era proposal removed (gregory, gregory-inverse, coptic, hebrew, ethiopic, ethioaa, saka, persian, mundi, minguo, before-roc, incarnation) and ASCII case variants of the codes are accepted, where CanonicalizeEraInCalendar admits Table 2's codes and aliases only (decision D4); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c12: row C12: an ISO month-day's year past 2^31 saturates to 2147483647, which is not a leap year, so 29 February is refused under reject and constrained to the 28th, where CalendarMonthDayToISOReferenceDate regulates against the year given (the milestone's integer narrowing, as it reaches a calendar field); correction, answered by SJL-10.5
# js-c13: row C13: a PlainMonthDay lends iso8601 as a calendar value, where ToTemporalCalendarIdentifier returns its [[Calendar]] (hebrew); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c15: row C15: toPlainYearMonth keeps the date's own ISO day in every calendar but ISO 8601, where CalendarYearMonthFromFields sets the reference day to the first of the calendar month; correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# js-c16: row C16: toPlainMonthDay builds the month-day without a calendar in the Gregorian family, so it and its with() are iso8601, where they keep the date's calendar; correction, answered by SJL-10.5
# js-c17: row C17: PlainMonthDay#toPlainDate reads a buddhist or roc year as an ISO year (2544-02-10, 0090-02-10), where it is the calendar's year (2001-02-10); correction, answered by SJL-10.5

# vm-r6: row R6: new PlainDate with a year of 2^53 + 2 or of 10^20 either sign, new PlainDateTime with 2^53 + 2 or 10^20, and new PlainMonthDay with a reference year of 10^20 end the invocation (ProfileFault/ProfileContractViolation), because the shared IsoCalendarMath.EpochDays precondition throws before the limit check, where CreateTemporalDate and CreateTemporalDateTime throw a RangeError; correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0078, decision D9), answered by SJL-10.4
